newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler recalls S-class Mercedes for repair.
newsitem.headline: Daimler recalls S-class Mercedes for repair.

text.p: German car maker Daimler-Benz AG on Friday said it was recalling its S-class Mercedes cars produced between June 1995 and December 1996 for free repairs after a defect was found in the front brakes.
Daimler said quality checks had found that in eight cars the front wheels at full lock had come into contact with the brake hose, posing the risk of damage to the braking system.
There had, however, been no accidents due to the fault.

"In none of the cars was there the risk of brake failure," the statement said, adding that a double circulation system would have ensured sufficient brake power even if there had been a leak in the brake hose.
Daimler said that the recall would affect 15,700 S-class limousines in Germany, a further 24,200 in the U.S. and Canada, 7,600 in Japan and a further 21,200 in other countries.
The company said that the repair would be free, and that new S-class models had already been fixed with parts to ensure that the front wheels and brake hoses did not come into contact.
